scores.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Tol palette with rank-encoded node colors, clean typographic hierarchy, and functional search/expand controls give it a polished, considered feel — but the lower half of the viewport is empty dead space, and the pink collapsed-count badges all render the same color regardless of rank, losing the encoding.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Tree layout is structurally honest with data-driven SVG dimensions and correct descendant counts, but uses weak name+depth string keys instead of stable unique IDs, risking visual corruption if node names collide; no quantitative encoding violations apply since circles encode categorical state (leaf vs. parent) rather than data magnitude.
scores.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() calls before new transitions so rapid node clicks or expand-all during a 500ms in-flight transition can cause jumping elements; all other checks pass (search is debounced 200ms, no brush/zoom update storm, no cross-view dispatch loops, no stale scale closures, pointer events used correctly avoiding mouse-touch fights).
scores.cognitive_load_note: Progressive disclosure manages ~200-node tree well: default 2-level view is clean with only 12 visible nodes, rank-color legend is compact and legible, and collapsed-node counts (+37, +43) give context without expanding; search-path highlighting would further reduce load during interaction, but cannot be verified from static screenshot.

proposer: Replaced the manual xMin/xMax loop with `d3.extent()` (saves 4 lines) and inlined the `hasKids` helper that was used only 3 times (saves 4 more lines). Net reduction: ~7 lines.
